title: A weekly day of quiet
hook: a half-day of mindfulness each week
tomorrow: Mai is broke all summer. can her weekly gift be time?

segments.voice: Yesterday was a weekly sit with others: every week, because meeting often came first on the Buddha's list. Today, the other end of the week: time with almost no one.

Sunday is the program's one day off. Jess, Mai's roommate, wants the art museum downtown, all day. Mai had pictured a quiet morning: no phone, no studio, no talking. Can a day be both? Inside Buddhism there are two honest answers to what a quiet day is, and each has good teachers behind it.
screen: `ONE DAY OFF.` → `THE MUSEUM, OR QUIET?` → `TWO HONEST ANSWERS.`

segments.voice: The first view: quiet means apart. The suttas show the Buddha himself stepping away. In one, he tells the monks he wants to go into seclusion for three months, and no one should come to him except the one who brings his alms food. Afterward he says: if anyone asks, tell them the Teacher spent the rains in mindfulness of breathing. The Pali word is viveka, seclusion. Its best case: you can't hear your own mind while the world keeps talking. A quiet day needs real edges: phone off, no plans, sitting and walking. The second view: quiet means slow, inside ordinary life. The Vietnamese teacher Thich Nhat Hanh taught a weekly day of mindfulness in which the chores still get done, washing dishes, sweeping, making tea, only slowly, each one done for itself and not to be finished with. Its best case: a quiet that exists only away from life won't survive Monday, so you practice where you live. Both views share the heart of it: some part of every week, set apart, so the mind can settle. They differ on where the edges go: around the day, or inside it. Mai's Sunday could hold both, a quiet morning with real edges, then an afternoon in the museum, looking at one painting long enough to see it. A quiet day isn't empty. It's unhurried.
screen: `APART: THE BUDDHA'S THREE MONTHS.` · `VIVEKA: REAL EDGES.` · `SLOW: CHORES DONE FOR THEMSELVES.` · `EDGES AROUND IT, OR INSIDE IT.` · then, large: `A QUIET DAY.`

segments.voice: Stand and walk very slowly across the room and back, as if this minute belonged to a quiet day. Feel each foot lift, move and land. Then sit for the rest of the time, and notice that the quiet came with you.
A weekly day of quiet: part of every week set apart, with edges around it or slowness inside it.
screen: `A WEEKLY DAY OF QUIET — today's word`.

segments.voice: Pocket this one: a quiet day, unhurried rather than empty, once every week. Sunday, kept.

howItsDone: Buddhists keep weekly quiet time in different ways: some set aside a half-day or day of silence, sitting and walking with phones off; communities in Thich Nhat Hanh's tradition keep a day of mindfulness with sitting, walking and chores done slowly.
